title.zh: 误译中诞生的太平洋失落大陆
title.en: The lost Pacific continent born of a mistranslation

summary.zh: 十九世纪学者误译玛雅抄本造出的"沉没之地"，经詹姆斯·丘奇沃德1926年的著作被搬进太平洋，成为神秘学中的失落大陆。
summary.en: A "sunken land" conjured from a nineteenth-century mistranslation of a Maya codex, relocated to the Pacific by James Churchward in 1926 and adopted by esoteric lore.

description.zh:
现代姆大陆传说的形成，与十九世纪对玛雅抄本的错误释读有关。1869至1870年，法国神甫布拉瑟·德·布尔堡刊布《特罗阿诺抄本》（今马德里抄本的一部分）的释读，误用兰达主教记录的"玛雅字母表"，从中"读出"一片毁于灾变的沉没之地，并将两个无法辨识的字符拼为其名"Mu"。摄影师奥古斯特·勒普隆冈随后宣称姆大陆的"莫皇后"逃亡埃及创建了尼罗河文明——他把这片大陆放在大西洋，与亚特兰蒂斯几乎重合。

1926年，英裔美国人詹姆斯·丘奇沃德出版《消失的姆大陆》，把故事彻底改写：他自称年轻时在印度一座寺庙里由高僧传授了解读"那迦尔石板"的秘法，得知太平洋中央曾横亘一块东西约八千公里的大陆，居民六千四百万，一万两千年前在火山与地陷中一夜沉没，复活节岛石像与波利尼西亚诸岛皆是残骸。这些主张未获得可独立核验的证据。

姆大陆应作为近代失落文明叙事来阅读，不能凭借故事中的地图与数字认定其存在。同时，也不能笼统声称太平洋没有被海水覆盖的大陆地壳：西南太平洋的西兰大陆（Zealandia）有地质研究支持，大部分位于水下。这项发现并不等于证实丘奇沃德描述的姆大陆及其文明。
description.en:
The modern Mu narrative developed through nineteenth-century misreadings of Maya texts. In 1869-70 the French abbé Brasseur de Bourbourg published a reading of the Troano Codex (part of the Madrid Codex) misusing Bishop Diego de Landa's recorded "Maya alphabet", claimed to find in it the record of a land destroyed by catastrophe, and assembled two undecipherable glyphs into its name, Mu. The photographer Augustus Le Plongeon then announced that Queen Móo of Mu had fled to Egypt and founded Nile civilization, placing the continent in the Atlantic, nearly on top of Atlantis.

In 1926 the Anglo-American writer James Churchward published The Lost Continent of Mu and rewrote the story wholesale. He claimed that as a young man in India a temple priest had taught him to read the "Naacal tablets", which revealed a continent some eight thousand kilometres wide spanning the central Pacific, home to sixty-four million people, swallowed overnight by volcanoes and collapsing land twelve thousand years ago; Easter Island's statues and the islands of Polynesia were its remnants. These claims lack independently verifiable evidence.

Mu belongs to modern lost-civilization literature; its maps and numerical claims do not establish its existence. Nor is it accurate to rule out all submerged continental crust in the Pacific: geological research supports Zealandia, a largely submerged continent in the southwest Pacific. That finding does not establish Churchward’s Mu or its civilization.
